To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the T-invariancy violation effects in the differential observables of pd scattering are of the same order of magnitude as the T-odd part of the interaction, (ii) the T-invariant relationships between differential observables are violated by 10% at the level of accuracy of the Glaube theory, and (iii) the T-invariace violation effects in the integral cross section are 10 times smaller than the effects in the differential spin observables.

(i) the degree to which relationships imposed on spin observables by T-invariance are violated is estimated to be of the order of the T-odd component of the interaction, and (ii) the degree to whch the T-odd effects are violated is of the same order as in the integral cross section for interaction between transversally polarized protons.

the violation of the T-invarianc relationships between the differential spin observables of the pd scattering is not expected to be large, while the violation of the relationships between the differential and integral spin observables of a null test experiment is expected to be large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a search for the T-invariancy violation effects in the spin observables of elastic pd-scatterings.
the search for a violation of the T-invariancy principle in the interaction of polarized protons with polarized deuterons.
the study of T-invariance violations in spin observables and integral cross section of elastic scattering pd→pd.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T-invarianve violation effects in spin observable are not observable with the existing experimental data.
the T-odd effects are small, but that the T-violation effects are not.
the null test experiment will be more effective than the experiment with spin observables in searching for T-invarance violation effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a violation of the T-invariancy in pd-scattering is not excluded.
, for the T-violation effects in the spin observables, the null test experiment is more sensitive than the experiment with the T-odd-P-even interaction.
the degree of T-invariance violations is comparable in both experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T-odd effect in elastic pd-scattering is small and is not observable at present.
the T-odd interaction in pd scattering is not large.
the degree to which T-invariance is violated in elastic pd scattering is much smaller than the corresponding estimate for a null-test experiment.
